messages:
maria: quick heads-up — bringing up a quantized Llama-2 small (8-bit) and seeing early termination in streaming for chat prompts. responses cut off mid-sentence, looks like EOS fired early.

aj: can you paste a minimal repro + the model's tokenizer/config.json you converted from HF?

maria: yup. repro: streaming chat with system+user template, prefix cache enabled. conversion used `hf-to-redwood` script. config.json excerpt:```
{
  "eos_token": "\u2592\u2592\u2592",
  "special_tokens_map": {
    "eos_token": "\u2592\u2592\u2592",
    "bos_token": "<|bos|>"
  },
  "chat_template": ["system", "user", "assistant"]
}
```
(we used a nonstandard sentinel for tests; HF model had multiple EOS-like added_tokens too)

kai: do you have tokenizer added_tokens / ids? sometimes multiple EOS tokens get squashed by the runtime.

maria: tokenizer.decode streaming chunk log:```
[stream chunk] tokens: [50256, 50256, 345, 78, 50256]
decoded: "\n"
```
The service stops after that second 50256 and returns blank. If I remove prefix-cache the stream continues normally.

aj: interesting — Redwood conversion maps HF `special_tokens_map` into a single EOS sentinel and also builds stop sequences from chat_template. I bet the conversion dedup step collapses repeated EOS tokens into one and sets a stop-pattern that matches early when it sees the first occurrence in streaming chunks.

\kai: +1. Also quantized runtime path uses a fast token-boundary check in the streaming loop: if token in eos_set -> flush. If eos_set built from deduped names but tokenizer returns multiple EOS ids (added_tokens with separate ids), the first match may not be intended (e.g., it's actually an internal placeholder).

tess: temporary workaround: pass explicit `stop` param in the API call to override the converted stop sequences. e.g.:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.run/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -d '{"model":"my-quant-l2","prompt":"...","stream":true,"stop":["\u2592\u2592\u2592"]}'
```
That forces the runtime not to treat other EOS ids as stop.

maria: confirmed — explicit stop fixes it for streaming. Not ideal for customers though.

aj: short-term fix idea: conversion script should preserve all token ids from `added_tokens` / `special_tokens_map` into the eos_set (instead of normalizing/deduping by string). Then runtime checks ids, not strings. Also make streaming loop ignore consecutive EOS tokens within a token-run if they appear at the same position in cache.

kai: agreed. I'll prototype: change conversion to emit `eos_token_ids: [50256, 50257]` into the model metadata. And update runtime's streaming early-exit to require either: (a) eos_id seen and following token is not eos_id within N lookahead, OR (b) user-supplied stop matched. That avoids tripping on double-sentinels coming from tokenizer quirks.

infra-bot: deploy notice: canary for eng-runtime updated with tag `fix/eos-id-check` queued for staging tests. :rocket:

aj: thanks. small follow-up: add a unit that simulates streaming chunks with repeated EOS ids and assert no early termination. Also add a quantized-mode test because the fast-path uses a different code path.

maria: I'll attach the model_id and quantization config to the issue. model: `org/ll2-small-quant8`, quant: `bits=8,group_size=64`. filing now.

kai: nice. open PR for conversion + runtime patch and we'll run canary. thx. :thumbsup:

maria: workaround note for docs: add explicit example showing `stop` override for chat-models converted from HF until fix ships.

aj: created issue RDW-ff-3287 and linked the canary job.

tess: thanks — marking this thread for follow-up in the onboarding checklist. :white_check_mark:
